issues.description: The problem specification and the template define a public method named singFarmSong() in Farm, but the reference solution implements this functionality under a differently-named public method playFarmSong(). This method-name mismatch means code or tests expecting singFarmSong() will not find it in the solution, and students comparing solution code to the specification or using the template Main (which calls singFarmSong()) will be confused or encounter missing-method issues.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution's public method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong() (and keep the private helper singFarmSongVerse(Animal) as is), or alternatively update the problem statement and template to use playFarmSong() consistently. Prefer renaming the solution method to singFarmSong() to match the specification and template.

issues.description: The problem statement and template specify a public Farm method named singFarmSong() (the task and UML refer to singFarmSong), but the solution implementation uses the name playFarmSong() for the same behavior. This naming divergence breaks the direct mapping between the required API and the provided solution (and even leaves a commented call to farm.singFarmSong() in Main), which will confuse students about which method to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or provide a public singFarmSong() wrapper that calls playFarmSong(). Ensure the solution Main (and any references) call singFarmSong() to match the problem statement and template API.
